key_insight: LLM stakeholder agents can generate healthcare decision weights, but deliberation and presentation-order bias can undermine their reliability.
engineering_relevance: Audit LLM-generated preferences and model their uncertainty before using them as weights in healthcare optimization.
method: Elicit explicit importance ratings for outpatient scheduling criteria from stakeholder-role agents.
Infer implicit trade-offs from pairwise choices between emergency department configurations.
Evaluate preference reliability and compare robust weighted-sum optimization with average-weight solutions.
evidence_signal: Computational experiments found role- and context-sensitive explicit ratings, strong presentation-order effects in pairwise choices, and robust solutions that differed from average-weight solutions in most cases.
watch_item: Role-prompted preferences should not be treated as validated stakeholder values; deliberation can erase role differences, and contextual predictors showed limited added predictive value beyond presentation order.
paper_title: On the possibilities and limitations of LLM-based multi-agent systems for multi-criteria decision-making in healthcare operations management
